blind_set_position.description: Move a blind to a position, in percent CLOSED (5536).

position.description: The wire value is percent CLOSED: 0 fully open, 100 fully closed, and `min`/`max` bound that raw value. `scale: -1` with `value_offset: 100` states the decoded terms, percent open (open = raw * -1 + 100), so a percent-open UI value encodes as raw = 100 - open: 75 % open sends 25.

blind_stop.description: Stop a moving blind by writing the trigger resource (5523).
blind_stop.notes: node-tradfri-client sends 5523 = 0.0 to stop; pytradfri (and so Home Assistant's stop_cover) sends 5523 = true. Both are reported to work; which value the gateway actually requires is not established.

factory_reset.advanced_reason: Erases every paired device, group, scene, schedule and issued PSK. Every bulb and accessory must be reset and paired again. There is no undo.
factory_reset.description: Reset the gateway to factory defaults (POST, empty body).

get_device.description: Read one device object (payload_formats.DeviceObject). Send with the Observe option set to 0 to subscribe instead of polling.

group_activate_scene.description: Recall a scene (mood) on a group. 5850 must be 1 for the scene to apply.

group_set_brightness.description: Set the dimmer level of every member of a group.

group_turn_off.description: Switch every member of a group off.

group_turn_on.description: Switch every member of a group on (flat object, no 3311 wrapper).

light_set_brightness.description: Set a light's dimmer level (5851). 0 turns the light off.

light_set_brightness_transition.description: Set the dimmer level with a fade (5712).

transition.description: Fade time; raw value is tenths of a second (10 = 1 s).

light_set_color_hex.description: Set a light to one of the gateway's preset colours by hex string (5706); see protocol_details.tradfri_coap.white_spectrum_hex.

hex.description: Six lowercase hex digits from the preset list, e.g. f1e0b5. Arbitrary RGB values are not honoured.

light_set_color_temperature.description: Set a white-spectrum light's colour temperature in mireds (5711).

id.description: Device id of a white-spectrum or colour light.

mireds.description: 250 is the coldest (about 4000 K), 454 the warmest (about 2200 K).

light_set_color_xy.description: Set a colour light by CIE 1931 xy (5709/5710).

id.description: Device id of a colour light.

list_devices.description: List device ids: answers a bare JSON array such as [65536,65537,65538]. Observe it to learn of added or removed devices.

list_scenes.description: List the scene ids belonging to a group.

reboot_gateway.advanced_reason: Drops every DTLS session and observation for about a minute; clients must reconnect and re-observe.

request_psk.description: Enrol a client: over a DTLS session opened with identity Client_identity and the label security code as PSK, POST the identity this client will use. The gateway answers 2.01 Created with that identity's PSK (9091) and its firmware version (9029).
request_psk.notes: The bootstrap session is used for this one request; reconnect with the new identity/PSK for everything else.

identity.description: Client-chosen identity, unique per installation (Home Assistant uses a random 32-hex-character UUID). Becomes the DTLS identity of every later session, so it is stored next to the PSK; see the setup stage's issues_credentials.identity.

set_commissioning_mode.description: Open the gateway for pairing remotes, dimmers and motion sensors for the given number of seconds (9061 on the gateway-info resource).

seconds.description: How long the gateway accepts new accessories.

txt_match.description: node-tradfri-client reads the gateway firmware from TXT `version`. A weak narrowing on a generic CoAP service type (see remaining_unknowns); it is what the schema can say.

methods.notes: node-tradfri-client browses _coap._udp and takes the instance name (matched as `gw-` followed by twelve lowercase hex digits, the gateway's MAC without separators — for example gw-aabbccddeeff), the SRV target host and the TXT `version` key (the gateway firmware). `_coap._udp` is a generic CoAP service type, so the gw- prefix is what makes a hit a TRÅDFRI gateway. Home Assistant instead discovers the gateway through its HomeKit advertisement (`_hap._tcp`, model TRADFRI) and keys it by the HomeKit `id` property; that is a second, independent signal.

device.name: IKEA TRÅDFRI Gateway (E1526)
device.notes:
The TRÅDFRI gateway is IKEA's first-generation Zigbee hub: a small Ethernet-only box that fronts TRÅDFRI bulbs, panels, control outlets, blinds, STARKVIND air purifiers and battery remotes. Its whole local API is CoAP (RFC 7252) secured with DTLS in pre-shared-key mode on UDP 5684 (coaps). There is no cloud dependency on that path: a client proves it holds the gateway's printed security code once, receives a per-client PSK, and from then on reads, writes and observes JSON resources named by LwM2M/IPSO-style numbers.
STATUS (as of 2026-10): IKEA's FAQ says no new products or features will be released for the gateway or the IKEA Home smart 1 app after April 2024, citing the gateway's memory limit, and that the system will be supported "at least until June 2026". Firmware did keep coming after that: the release notes list gateway 1.21.44 (1 July 2025), 1.21.51 (10 February 2026) and 1.21.57 (4 May 2026, bug fixes), the last of which is the image IKEA's OTA feed still offers. The successor is the DIRIGERA hub (October 2022), which speaks a different API; the new IKEA Home smart app does not talk to this gateway at all. This spec is for owners who keep the gateway after that window, or who want to drive it without either app.
RESOURCE MODEL: everything is a GET/PUT/POST on a numbered path, carrying a UTF-8 JSON object whose keys are decimal strings. 15001 is the device list, 15004 groups, 15005 scenes ("moods"), 15010 smart tasks, 15011 the gateway itself. A collection GET answers a bare JSON array of instance ids; a GET on one id answers that instance's object. Writes are PUTs of a partial object. Device control rides inside a one-element array under the device-kind key (3311 lights, 3312 outlets, 15015 blinds, 15025 air purifiers); group control is flat. See payload_formats and protocol_details.tradfri_coap.

openness.notes: IKEA never published the API. The resource and key numbers were worked out by the community from captures of the vendor app and are now stable across a decade of open-source clients. Many of the device-level numbers (3311 Light Control, 3312 Power Control, 5850 On/Off, 5851 Dimmer, 5706 Colour, 5712 Transition Time) are borrowed from the OMA LwM2M/IPSO registry; the 9xxx and 15xxx numbers are IKEA's own. IKEA does tolerate third-party clients to the extent of asking them (per node-tradfri-client's README) not to store the security code — only the issued identity and PSK.

issued_to_client: DTLS PSK (string, from 9091) for the client-chosen identity sent in 9090
credentials.notes: The security code is a long-lived bootstrap secret printed on the hardware: anyone who can read the label and reach UDP 5684 can enrol a client. glenndehaan's notes report that an issued PSK expires if it goes unused for six weeks and that each use extends it; a client that has been idle that long should be ready to re-enrol. Use `<security-code>` / `<psk>` placeholders in any notes; never commit a real one.
stored_on_device: Zigbee network key and the paired device table

factory_reset.description: The E1526 manual gives a pinhole on top of the gateway, under the removable lid. The same reset is reachable over the API as commands.factory_reset.
factory_reset.effect: Erases every paired Zigbee device, group, scene, smart task and every issued client identity/PSK. Bulbs and accessories stay joined to a network that no longer exists and must be reset and paired again. Never needed for a lost PSK — re-enrol with the security code instead, which costs nothing.

procedures.basis: IKEA TRÅDFRI gateway manual (E1526), Factory reset section.
procedures.name: Pinhole under the lid

steps.action: Lift off the gateway's lid and push a pin into the pinhole on top for at least 5 seconds.
Wait for the gateway to restart.

methods.description: Two things in order: the gateway joins the LAN over its Ethernet port, then the client enrols once with the security code to obtain its own identity/PSK pair. No vendor account or app is involved in either step.
methods.name: Ethernet, then enrol with the label security code

stages.description: Connect the gateway's Ethernet port to the router and power it from its USB supply. It takes a DHCP lease and starts answering on UDP 5684. A DHCP reservation is recommended by Home Assistant, because a moved address breaks stored hosts.
stages.name: Put the gateway on the LAN

steps.action: Connect the gateway to the router with Ethernet and power it.
steps.expect: The gateway's front LEDs settle and it answers mDNS _coap._udp as gw-<mac>.

stages.description: The physical proof here is the label rather than a button: the 16-character security code (case-sensitive; Home Assistant warns about I/l confusion) is the PSK for the bootstrap identity "Client_identity". Over that DTLS session the client POSTs the identity it will use from now on and the gateway answers 2.01 Created with that identity's PSK. commands.request_psk is this call.

identity.notes: Not issued by the gateway: the client names itself, sends the name as 9090 in request_psk, and must store it with the PSK, because every later DTLS session presents it. Any string unique to this install works; a client may fill it for the owner (a random 32-hex string, as Home Assistant does) rather than asking. The schema has no "client-generated" credential kind, so it is declared user_entered.

psk.notes: The DTLS pre-shared key for the identity sent in 9090, used as UTF-8 bytes. Store identity and PSK together, keyed by the gateway's mDNS name or gateway id (9081), not its IP. The matching identity is not returned: it is the 9090 value the client itself sent, so store that too. Clients use something unique per install (Home Assistant a random 32-hex UUID, node-tradfri-client "tradfri_" plus a millisecond timestamp).

stages.name: Enrol this client with the security code

steps.action: Read the 16-character security code from the label on the underside of the gateway.
Open a DTLS-PSK session to UDP 5684 with identity Client_identity and the security code as the key, then POST {"9090":"<identity>"} to /15011/9063.
steps.expect: 2.01 Created with a JSON body carrying 9091 (the PSK) and 9029 (gateway firmware version).

arguments.description: The identity this client will use from now on.

steps.action: Close that session and open a new one with identity <identity> and the returned PSK; GET /15011/15012 to confirm.
steps.expect: 2.05 Content with the gateway-info object (9029 firmware, 9081 gateway id).

setup.notes: The gateway reaches the LAN over Ethernet (it has no Wi-Fi client radio and nothing to provision), so the only protocol step is client enrolment: a DTLS handshake keyed by the 16-character security code printed on the label under the gateway, followed by one POST that returns a PSK for an identity the client chose. Every later session uses that identity and PSK; the security code is not needed again and should not be stored. Gateway firmware older than 1.2.42 accepted the security code directly as the PSK for every client; current firmware requires the enrolment.

rejoin.notes: Moving the gateway to another router is a cable move and a new DHCP lease. Issued identities survive, so clients only need the new address; find it again by the gw-<mac> mDNS name.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Every resource path, key number and payload is transcribed from open-source clients (pytradfri, node-tradfri-client) and the community coap-client walk-through, which agree on the paths and key numbers; where they differ (the blind stop value, the xy scale, the dimmer minimum) is in value_ranges and remaining_unknowns.

entities.name: TRÅDFRI Light
entities.notes: One entity per light (device type 5750 = 2). Enumeration is two-step — list_devices answers a bare array of ids and each id must be read on its own — which the `instances` block (an object keyed by id) cannot yet express, so the bound commands carry `instance:id` and a client supplies ids from list_devices. Brightness is 0-254. Colour temperature binds only for white-spectrum bulbs (those reporting 5711); xy and hex colour are documented as commands but not bound, because no consumer resolves a two-value set_color yet. Prefer observing get_device over polling it.

entities.name: TRÅDFRI Control Outlet
entities.notes: One per outlet (5750 = 3). Same two-step enumeration as the light.

entities.name: TRÅDFRI Blind
entities.notes: One per blind (5750 = 7; FYRTUR, KADRILJ, PRAKTLYSING, TREDANSEN). Position on the wire is percent CLOSED, and the two directions differ: the state read here (5536) is RAW percent closed, so a percent-open cover shows 100 minus it, but set_cover_position already takes percent OPEN (its parameter declares scale -1 / value_offset 100), so the client sends the UI value as-is and must not invert it a second time. Battery is under 3."9".

entities.name: TRÅDFRI Group
entities.notes: One per group from list_groups. The state shown is what was last set on the group, not an aggregate of its members — read the members for truth. Scenes are recalled with group_activate_scene.

entities.name: Accessory Battery
entities.notes: Remotes, motion sensors and blinds report battery percent under device-info key 3 -> 9. Remotes push nothing else useful.

evidence.documentation_review: pytradfri (master, read 2026-10-18), node-tradfri-client (master) and glenndehaan/ikea-tradfri-coap-docs agree on every path and key number used here (they differ on the blind stop value, the xy scale and the dimmer minimum; see remaining_unknowns); Home Assistant's integration source confirms the identity scheme and the cover inversion, and openHAB's binding docs the code-then-discard enrolment. IKEA's release notes and OTA feed (fetched 2026-10-18) give the gateway firmware history; the latest image offered is 1.21.57, released 4 May 2026.
evidence.open_questions: The DTLS cipher suite the gateway negotiates; whether an identity can be re-enrolled or has a length limit; the true idle-expiry rule for a PSK; the blind stop value (0 vs true); what 9054/9066/6 codes mean.
evidence.status_correction: The backlog entry said IKEA stopped updating the gateway in July 2024. IKEA's own FAQ dates the end of new products and features to April 2024 and promises support at least until June 2026; the release notes show further gateway firmware in July 2025, February 2026 and May 2026. "July 2024" matches only a bulb-firmware release (11 and 16 July 2024), not the gateway.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder only, to satisfy the schema's access-surface rule. The gateway serves no HTTP; its API is CoAP over DTLS on UDP 5684 (see `commands`, whose entries carry `transport: coap`, and protocol_details.tradfri_coap).
http_endpoints.name: Local API Placeholder

DeviceObject.description: One device, as GET /15001/<id> returns it and observe pushes it. The common keys are always present; exactly one device-kind array (3311, 3312, 15015, 15025, 3300 for sensors) carries the controllable state, as a one-element array in every observed device. Values below are an invented example of a colour-temperature bulb.

fields.description: Instance id (integer, the same id as in the path).
Name the owner gave the device (string).
Reachable: 1 reachable, 0 not. A bulb switched off at the wall keeps its last state here with 9019 = 0.
OTA update state (integer; codes not documented).
Device info object: "0" manufacturer, "1" model number, "2" serial, "3" firmware version, "6" power source (integer code), "9" battery percent 0-100 on battery devices.

Light control array (lights only). Each element: 5850 on/off (0/1), 5851 dimmer 0-254, 5706 colour hex string, 5707 hue, 5708 saturation, 5709 colour x, 5710 colour y, 5711 colour temperature in mireds, 5712 transition time (tenths of a second, write-only).
Outlet array: 5850 on/off, 5851 dimmer (no dimmable outlet is known).
Blind array: 5536 position (float, 0 open to 100 closed), 5523 trigger (write; used to stop a moving blind).

Air purifier array: 5900 fan mode (0 off, 1 auto, 10/20/30/40/50 levels 1-5), 5908 fan speed, 5905 controls locked, 5906 status LEDs off, 5907 air quality (PM2.5), 5903 filter status, 5902 filter runtime, 5904 filter lifetime, 5910 filter remaining, 5909 motor runtime.

parse_rules: Parse as JSON. Keys are decimal strings; look up the device kind by which of 3311 / 3312 / 15015 / 15025 / 3300 is present (or by 5750).
Take element [0] of the kind array; no shipped TRÅDFRI device is reported to carry more than one.
Treat a missing colour key as 'not supported by this bulb' rather than zero: dimmable-only bulbs carry no 5706/5711, colour bulbs carry 5707-5710.
Honour 9019 before drawing a live control.

fields.description: Gateway id (string); a stable key for stored credentials.
Commissioning mode (write a number of seconds to open pairing for accessories).
First-setup time, Unix epoch seconds (meaning inferred by pytradfri).

GroupObject.description: One group, as GET /15004/<id> returns it. The gateway reports the group's own last-set values, not an aggregate of its members.

fields.description: On/off last set on the group.
Dimmer last set on the group, 0-254.
Id of the scene last activated.

parse_rules: Do not use the group's 5850/5851 as the state of its lights; read the members. node-tradfri-client notes the gateway does not report group properties back after a change.

fields.description: The PSK for the enrolled identity (string).

device_types.description: Key 5750 on a device object (node-tradfri-client's table; pytradfri names 7 as blind).

dtls_credentials.bootstrap: identity `Client_identity`, PSK = the 16-character security code as UTF-8 bytes; valid only for POST /15011/9063
dtls_credentials.session: identity = the 9090 string the client enrolled, PSK = the 9091 string returned, as UTF-8 bytes

tradfri_coap.observe: Every collection and instance is observable (RFC 7641): a GET carrying the Observe option with value 0 registers, the first response is the current state, and each later notification on the same token is the complete new object. pytradfri and node-tradfri-client observe each device id under 15001 and each group under 15004; they also observe 15001 itself to learn of added and removed devices. Battery remotes and sensors are reported not to push useful events (Home Assistant and openHAB both say so), so observe is for lights, outlets, blinds and purifiers. After a gateway reboot or network loss, observations are lost and must be re-registered on a fresh DTLS session.
tradfri_coap.response_codes: Clients check 2.05 Content on GET and 2.01 Created on the PSK POST; PUTs answer 2.04 Changed. A 4.04 on a device id means it was removed. Libraries treat a DTLS handshake failure after a gateway firmware update as "re-enrol": Home Assistant documents "Fatal DTLS error: code 115" after updates and code 20 for a wrong security code.

roots.15001: Devices. GET -> array of device ids (five digits, from 65536).
roots.15004: Groups. GET -> array of group ids (six digits, from 131072). PUT /15004/add and /15004/remove with {"9038": <group id>, "9003": [<device id>]} edit membership.
roots.15005: Scenes, called moods before app 1.12. GET /15005/<group id> -> scene ids for that group (six digits, around 196608); GET /15005/<group id>/<scene id> -> one scene.
roots.15009: Remote controls (pytradfri constant; unused by the clients).
roots.15011: Gateway. /15011/15012 info (GET, observe, PUT), /15011/9063 PSK enrolment (POST), /15011/9030 reboot (POST), /15011/9031 factory reset (POST), /15011/9034 firmware update trigger.

tradfri_coap.transport: CoAP (RFC 7252) over DTLS in PSK mode, UDP port 5684, URI scheme coaps://<gateway>:5684/<path>. Payloads are UTF-8 JSON with decimal-string keys. pytradfri drives it with aiocoap (tinydtls); node-tradfri-client with its own node-dtls-client; the community walk-through with libcoap's coap-client built with DTLS.

value_ranges.blind_5536: 0-100, percent CLOSED: 0 is fully open, 100 fully closed. Home Assistant and node-tradfri-client both present 100 minus it.
value_ranges.colour_xy_5709_5710: CIE 1931 x and y scaled to 0-65535 (pytradfri); node-tradfri-client scales by 65279.
value_ranges.dimmer_5851: 0-254 (not the IPSO 0-100). pytradfri allows 0, which turns the light off; the coap-client notes give 1-254 as the dimming range.
value_ranges.hue_5707_saturation_5708: Hue 0-65535; saturation 0-65279 (pytradfri: higher is accepted but produces no light).
value_ranges.mireds_5711: 250-454 on white-spectrum bulbs (pytradfri and node-tradfri-client agree); about 4000 K to 2200 K.
value_ranges.transition_5712: Tenths of a second (node-tradfri-client converts seconds x 10).

tradfri_coap.white_spectrum_hex: Colour-temperature bulbs also accept the fixed 5706 hex strings f5faf6 (cold), f1e0b5 (normal) and efd275 (warm); newer bulb firmware (about 2.3.087 on) adds f3f3e3 and f2eccf. The coap-client notes report that an unlisted hex falls back to a warm glow, and that bulb firmware 2.3.086 instead turned the bulb off while reporting it on. For colour bulbs prefer 5709/5710 (xy) over the hex presets.

remaining_unknowns: DTLS cipher suite and version: the clients delegate to tinydtls, node-dtls-client and libcoap and none of the sources here names the suite the gateway selects. TLS_PSK_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8 is commonly assumed for CoAP but is not confirmed.
PSK lifetime: the six-weeks-idle expiry is from one community write-up; neither library implements or documents it.
Identity rules: maximum length, permitted characters, how many identities the gateway keeps, and what POSTing an already-enrolled identity returns are undocumented.
Blind stop: node-tradfri-client writes 5523 = 0.0, pytradfri writes true; which the gateway requires (or whether any write to 5523 stops it) is not established.
Whether firmware 1.21.57 (May 2026) or any later release changes the API, and whether IKEA will keep the OTA feed online after the June 2026 support floor.

Discovery narrowing: `_coap._udp` is every CoAP device that advertises itself, and the TXT `version` key the method requires is a weak signal. The decisive check is the instance name (`gw-` followed by twelve hex digits), which the schema has no matcher for; a client should apply it before treating a hit as this gateway.
Cover position: the entity's state (5536) is raw percent closed while blind_set_position takes percent open; entity-level `scale` cannot carry the offset that would make the two agree.
Codes for 9054 (OTA state), 9066 (OTA type), 9071 (time source) and device-info 6 (power source) are not documented by the clients.

The `instances` block cannot express a hub whose collection GET answers an array of ids (each child read separately), so the entities rely on `instance:id` without `instances`; a schema field for two-step enumeration would fix this.

The schema has no CoAP transport block, so commands carry `transport: coap` with `method`/`path`/`body` and the DTLS session rules live in protocol_details.tradfri_coap; the placeholder http_endpoints entry exists only to satisfy the access-surface rule.
